title: She Announced Her Pregnancy. Forty-Eight Hours Later, She Was Fighting Shah Rukh Khan.
excerpt: Deepika Padukone is expecting baby number two — and somehow still the hardest-working person on two of Bollywood's biggest sets.
body:
Somewhere inside the sprawling Golden Tobacco Studio in Mumbai's Vile Parle, there's a set where Deepika Padukone and Shah Rukh Khan spent two days choreographing a stylised combat sequence against eight fighters. The kind of scene that would leave most actors breathless on a good week. Deepika filmed it on April 21 and 22 — roughly forty-eight hours after telling the world she's pregnant with her second child.

That's the kind of woman we're dealing with.

The announcement itself was classic Deepika: understated, intimate, devastating in its simplicity. On April 19, she posted a single photograph of daughter Dua Padukone Singh clutching a positive pregnancy test — tiny hands, two pink lines, no caption beyond a pair of evil-eye emojis. Ranveer Singh co-posted it. The internet melted. Bollywood's comments section turned into a group hug. And then, before anyone had finished processing the news, Deepika was back on set in combat boots.

Two Blockbusters, One Pregnancy, Zero Excuses

Here's what makes Deepika's current workload genuinely staggering: she isn't just making one film. She's holding down two of the most expensive productions in Indian cinema simultaneously.

King, directed by Siddharth Anand, pairs her with Shah Rukh Khan in what's shaping up to be a massive Christmas 2026 tentpole — alongside debutante Suhana Khan and Abhishek Bachchan as the villain. The production has been meticulously calibrated around her pregnancy. All of Deepika's major action and climax sequences were designed to wrap by mid-May, while she was still in her first trimester. After the Mumbai leg, she flew to South Africa for a crucial climax setpiece, then returned for an elaborate sequence on a massive sandy backdrop at a studio in Mira Road. Her close-up shots will be seamlessly integrated with stunt footage through advanced VFX. The script? Untouched. Not a single scene has been cut or rewritten because of the pregnancy.

Then there's Raka — director Atlee's next spectacle after the earth-scorching *Jawan*, starring Allu Arjun fresh off the *Pushpa* phenomenon. Deepika has roughly 50 days of shooting remaining, and her character reportedly features a spectacular entry sequence and a major action-packed confrontation alongside Allu Arjun. The moment Atlee heard the pregnancy news, according to an exclusive Bollywood Hungama report, he was overjoyed — and immediately sat down with his creative team to draft what insiders are calling "Plan B." A body double will handle the most physically demanding stunt work, with Deepika's already-filmed close-ups stitched in through VFX during the final edit. Her role stays fully intact. Nothing deleted, nothing softened.

The Woman Who Walked Away — and the Woman Who Stayed

Here's the context that makes all of this hit differently. Late last year, Deepika made headlines for exiting two high-profile projects — Kalki 2 and Sandeep Reddy Vanga's Spirit — after reportedly requesting a maximum 7-to-8-hour workday, a boundary the productions declined to accommodate. The decision sparked a massive industry debate about work-life balance, with plenty of people lining up on both sides.

And now? She's managing two simultaneous mega-productions, a pregnancy, and the kind of schedule that would flatten most actors who never set boundaries at all. The difference isn't that Deepika won't work hard. It's that she chooses where to invest that energy — and when a director and production house meet her halfway, she shows up with everything she has.

> "The dedication of the global icon is further evidenced by her recent activity on the sets of King. Despite her pregnancy announcement, Deepika was back on the grind within forty-eight hours." — Bollywood Hungama

That's not stubbornness. That's leverage — earned through a career that includes Pathaan, Jawan, and the kind of global stardom that makes studios rearrange their entire production calendars around you rather than the other way around.

Where to Watch

*King* is locked for a worldwide theatrical release on Christmas 2026 — expect it across screens in the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf on day one, with a major OTT streaming window to follow. *Raka* is currently tracking for a 2027 release and will almost certainly receive a simultaneous global rollout, given Allu Arjun's massive post-*Pushpa* international fanbase. For the diaspora, both films promise the kind of event-cinema experience worth booking opening-weekend tickets for.

Deepika Padukone is 40, expecting her second child, and starring opposite two of the biggest male leads in Indian cinema at the same time. She isn't slowing down. She's just picking her battles with surgical precision — and winning every single one.
